Natty describes someone who looks neat, smart, and stylish — particularly in the way they are dressed.

When you call a person natty, you're saying they look carefully and attractively put-together. Not just clean, not just tidy, but dressed in a way that shows good taste and visible effort. Picture someone wearing a well-fitted blazer, perfectly pressed trousers, a coordinated tie, and polished shoes. That is a natty look.

Natty sits right at the crossing point of two qualities: neatness and style. You need both for the word to apply.

  • Just being clean and tidy makes you neat — but not natty.
  • Just being fashionable makes you stylish — but not natty.
  • Being both at the same time, in a precise and pleasing way, makes you natty.

There's also a quiet sense of care and intention behind the word. A natty person hasn't accidentally stumbled into looking good. They've paid attention to their appearance, and it shows.
The feel and tone of the word

Natty is a warm, slightly old-fashioned word. It almost always works as a genuine compliment, and it often carries a gentle sense of admiration — sometimes even affection, as if you're charmed by how well someone is turned out.

It has a mildly playful quality too. Calling someone natty feels more cheerful and personal than calling them "well-dressed," which is more neutral and formal.

This is important for using the word correctly:

  • Not expensive. A natty person doesn't need to wear luxury brands. Someone in a modest but perfectly coordinated outfit can be completely natty. The word is about how the clothes work together, not what they cost.
  • Not flashy or showy. Natty is about crisp, smart elegance — not bold, head-turning fashion. A person dripping in loud colours and oversized accessories would not typically be called natty.
  • Not just clean. Being clean is a basic expectation. Being natty is a compliment that goes well beyond that.
Natty applied to things, not just people

You can also use natty to describe clothing and accessories on their own, without referring to the full person. In this case, it means the item itself looks neat, well-made, and attractive.

  • "a natty little bow tie"
  • "a natty blazer"
  • "a natty pair of shoes"

In each case, the item looks smart and pleasing — precisely the kind of thing a natty person would wear.

• He showed up to the dinner looking remarkably natty in a grey suit and a pale yellow pocket square.
  • For someone who had been travelling all day, she looked surprisingly natty.
  • I see you're wearing that natty hat again — it suits you.
  • The professor was known for his natty appearance: always a crisp shirt, always a well-knotted tie.
  • She paired the simple dress with a natty little scarf that tied the whole look together.
How natty compares to similar words

Dapper is the closest word in meaning — both describe someone who is smartly and neatly dressed. The main difference is that dapper is used almost exclusively for men, while natty can describe anyone regardless of gender.

Spruce (as in "looking spruce") is another close word, meaning neat and tidy in appearance — but it focuses more on tidiness and less on style. Natty implies more flair.

Smart (especially in British English) also means well-dressed, but it's a broader and more neutral word. Natty is more specific and carries more personality and warmth.

Dashing suggests exciting, impressive attractiveness — it's a stronger, more dramatic word than natty, and is less about neat precision.
One other meaning (a separate, less common usage)

In Jamaican and Caribbean culture — particularly in reggae music and Rastafarian traditions — natty is used to describe natural, unprocessed hair, especially dreadlocks. You may have heard the phrase "natty dread." This is a completely separate meaning rooted in a specific cultural context, and it is not what the word means in everyday mainstream English.

If you come across "natty" outside of that specific cultural context, it almost certainly refers to the neat-and-stylish meaning described throughout this explanation.
